meta.title: Ori: a goal that survives a bad week
meta.description: Ori is an AI self-development coach. It lays your goal into your calendar and, when a bad week hits, rebuilds the plan. Joining the waitlist costs nothing, and we start in the Czech Republic and Slovakia.
meta.og_description: AI can build your plan. Ori keeps it alive when it falls apart.

seo.org_description: Ori is a startup from the Czech Republic building an AI self-development coach. The app lays a goal into your calendar and, when the plan starts to break, rebuilds it around the user's real capacity and energy.
seo.app_alt: AI self-development coach and adaptive goal planner
seo.app_description: Ori is an AI self-development coach for Android and iPhone. It turns a goal into a route of milestones and plans the steps into your real calendar. When the plan starts to break, Ori notices, reaches out first, and makes tasks smaller or different based on current capacity and energy, not just later. The app is in testing; access opens step by step through a waitlist, first in the Czech Republic and Slovakia.
features: A twenty-minute setup that turns a goal into a route of milestones
Plans the steps around your real calendar
Notices when you go quiet and reaches out first
Reads your capacity from skipped steps
Makes tasks smaller or different, not just later
No pile of unfinished tasks waiting after a bad week
Plans by energy, to prevent burnout
Several goals planned together within your capacity
See your data, download it and delete it at any time
seo.audience: People whose plans keep running into real life: young professionals (25 to 35) and high performers who have burned out before.
seo.keywords: AI coach, personal development, goal app, goal planning, adaptive plan, habits, burnout prevention, achieving goals
seo.damian: Co-founder and CEO of Ori. Product strategy, business development, marketing and fundraising.
seo.jindrich: Co-founder and CTO of Ori. Product vision, AI, design and UX/UI.

hero.who: For people whose plans keep running into real life.
hero.h1: A goal that survives a bad week.
hero.lede: Tell Ori what you want to achieve. In twenty minutes you have the route to it laid into your calendar. And when a week comes that you can't keep up with, Ori rebuilds the plan. It doesn't wait for you to come back to a pile of tasks.
hero.note: Joining costs nothing. We start in the Czech Republic and Slovakia. A short email from Damian arrives right away. Privacy policy

phone.label: An example of Ori re-planning a day
phone.says: Heavy week at work. Your long run moves to Saturday morning. Tonight, 15 minutes of mobility keeps the streak alive.

week.label: A week where the plan falls apart: a new plan on Monday, a meeting breaks it on Wednesday, by Sunday there is a pile and a new plan.
captions: New plan. This time it will work.
The meeting ran long. Tomorrow, then.
Friends. No point even opening it.
items: On Sunday evening you write the plan for the week. By Wednesday a meeting runs long and it's over.
After work you have no energy left even to decide where to start. So you open Instagram.
One skipped workout. A week later it is a skipped month.
The app waits until you come back to a pile of unfinished tasks. So you would rather not come back.
This is the third time this year you're starting this goal.
week.statement: You're not someone who doesn't finish things. Your plan just assumed you'd be the same person every week.

band.label: What broke the plan this year:

jak.h2: When you leave the route, Ori recalculates it.
jak.lede: A typical app moves your task to tomorrow. Tomorrow it is there again, only bigger. Ori does what the navigation in your car does. It notices you are off the route and finds a new one. A smaller step instead of a big one. Saturday instead of Thursday. The same goal.
jak.p1_p: When you go quiet for a few days, Ori reaches out first. You don't have to report that it isn't going well.
jak.p2_h: It shrinks it, or changes it.
jak.p2_p: It doesn't only change the date. It makes the scope smaller or picks a different activity you can manage today.
jak.p3_h: You carry on from where you are.
jak.p3_p: The same goal, a new route. The pile of unfinished tasks never shows up.
jak.step1: Tap "Low". You have no energy today.
jak.step2: Tick off the smaller step Ori suggested.
jak.step3: Open the Roadmap. The goal is still on track.
jak.done: That's what Ori does every day. So you don't have to.

kdo.h2: We're building what we were missing.
kdo.p1: We're two students. We've each started side projects before, and we ran into the same thing. The plan was ready in an evening. It fell apart the first week something else came up.
kdo.p2: We looked for an app that expects this. None of them fit. When we talked to friends, they said they needed something like it too. So we said: we are doing this.
kdo.p3: More people backed us than we expected. We talked the idea through with people from the field and validated it through JIC and Red Bull Basement. Now we are testing Ori with a first group of people.

faq.title: Questions - Ori
faq.description: Answers to the common questions about Ori: when it launches, what it costs, what it runs on and what happens to your data.

items.q: When does Ori launch, and when do I get access?
items.a: Ori is in testing now and there's no exact launch date yet. We'll open access step by step, in the Czech Republic and Slovakia first - people on the waitlist get it among the first.
We're still settling the pricing. As soon as it's clear, the waitlist hears first.
Android and iPhone. Our testers already use it on both.

items.q: What language is the app in?
items.a: English for now. Czech and Slovak are on the way.

items.q: How is it different from ChatGPT, Notion or Todoist?
items.a: ChatGPT writes you a plan, then stops watching whether it's working. Notion and Todoist are lists you manage yourself. Ori lays the plan into your calendar, notices when it starts to break, and rebuilds it around what you have in you right now - not just a day later, but smaller or different.

items.q: What does Ori know about me, and what does it do with it?
items.a: Only what it needs to plan: your goals, your plan, what you've done and how it went. In the app you can see what Ori knows about you, download your data, and delete it along with your whole account at any time. We don't sell your data and we don't train AI on it.

items.q: How much time does it take a day?
items.a: Setting up takes about twenty minutes, once. After that, a glance in the morning at what the day holds is enough. The rest of the time belongs to the steps themselves - and Ori sizes them to the time and energy you really have.

items.q: What kind of goals is Ori for?
items.a: Goals that take regular work over weeks or months: passing a language exam, running a half-marathon, starting a side project, learning a new skill. If a goal is still vague ("get fit"), Ori helps you make it concrete. It isn't a replacement for therapy or medical care.

items.q: What if I drop out completely for a week or two?
items.a: That's fine - Ori expects it. It notices the silence, reaches out first and rebuilds the plan, with no backlog waiting for you. You carry on from where you are: same goal, different path.

items.q: Can I have more than one goal at a time?
items.a: Yes. Ori plans them together, so they don't fight over the same time or go beyond your capacity.

faq.cta_p: Write to us at oriapp.eu@gmail.com - a person answers, not a bot.

privacy.title: Privacy policy - Ori
privacy.description: How Ori handles the email address you give us when you join the waitlist.
privacy.collect_p: When you join the waitlist, we keep your email address, the time you joined and the language of the page - so we write to you in Czech, Slovak or English. Nothing else - the form has no other fields.
privacy.why_p1: To thank you for joining (one short email, right after), to tell you when early access to Ori is ready for you, and about Ori's launch. We don't sell or share your address, and we don't send you anything unrelated to Ori.
privacy.why_p2: We process it because you asked us to (your consent, GDPR Art. 6(1)(a)). You can withdraw that at any time.
privacy.visits_p: We count visits to this website with Umami, an analytics service built for privacy: we see which pages were viewed, where a visit came from (a link on LinkedIn, say), the country and the type of device. It uses no cookies, builds no profile of you and does not store your IP address, so we can't tell from it who you are. We also count how many people join the waitlist - without the addresses themselves. We do this on the basis of our legitimate interest in knowing whether the website works (GDPR Art. 6(1)(f)).
privacy.where_p: In a database run for us by Supabase, our database provider. Emails are sent through Resend, our email provider. The page's fonts are served by this website itself.
privacy.long_p: Until you ask us to remove it, or until we no longer need it to invite you - after Ori's public launch we clear the list.
privacy.rights_p: You can ask us what we hold about you, ask us to correct it, or ask us to delete it - write to oriapp.eu@gmail.com from the address you signed up with and we'll do it. If you think we've handled your data wrongly, please tell us first at the same address - we'll look into it and put it right. You also always have the right to complain to the Czech data protection authority, the Úřad pro ochranu osobních údajů.
privacy.app_p: This page covers only this website and its waitlist. Once you use the Ori app itself, its own privacy policy applies, which you see when you create an account.
